attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post, stated as his own view.

semantics.note: 'Obviously not going to be here this year' is an unhedged forecast that AGI will not arrive in 2025. The remark about Musk and motives is correctly left out.

contract.note: Marcus gave no definition. Reading AGI as broad, flexible human-level competence is the ordinary meaning, not stretched either way. 'This year' as calendar 2025 is right.

evidence.note: ARC Prize organisers said in December 2025 that AGI was 'not yet' here. That is a few weeks before the deadline, but late enough to bear on 2025.
January 2026 technical report looking back on 2025 progress. It finds flaws that still have to be overcome to reach AGI.
Five-minute Turing test result. It shows conversational imitation, not broad general competence.
A competing scholarly claim that current LLMs already are AGI. It is an argument from a contested definition, not an independently established 2025 arrival.

reviews.rationale: The deadline (31 Dec 2025) has passed. Independent assessments from late 2025 and early 2026 find that systems were still materially short of broad human-level competence. The opposing claims (the Turing test result and the UCSD essay) rest on weaker or contested thresholds and do not meet the contract's contradiction standard.

attribution.note: Marcus's own characterisation of podcasters, in his own post.

semantics.note: The scope (a lot of prominent podcasters, Amodei's dates) and the word 'largely' are kept. 'Pulled out of hats' is figurative but implies a checkable lack of grounding.

contract.note: Reading 'as fact' as presenting uncertain timelines as settled, rather than merely not pushing back, is ordinary and fair. Requiring a reasonably broad set of transcripts suits a claim about a pattern.

evidence.note: Third-party transcript of Hard Fork, labelled as such. The host frames 'couple years away' as a hypothetical, which undercuts Marcus's main example. It is one episode only.
Original Lex Fridman transcript. Amodei hedges explicitly, and the host asks for numbers without stating them as fact. It does not show a pattern either way.

reviews.rationale: The packet has only two interviews. One weakens Marcus's cited Hard Fork example, but neither shows how common factual endorsement was among prominent podcasters. Nothing assesses whether the dates lacked a substantive basis. The evidence does not settle the pattern claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words about Amodei's timelines.

semantics.note: The 'mostly' qualifier and the move from 2025-2026 to 2026-2027 are both kept. 'Quietly' is kept too.

contract.note: Requiring comparable capability thresholds is what 'slipped back' ordinarily means: postponing the same prediction. That reading is fair.

evidence.note: The 2023 baseline. A hedged 'could' about conversational, educated-human-like ability, with higher thresholds explicitly said to come later.
Amodei's own January 2025 post confirms he talks of 2026-2027. However, those dates apply to AI smarter than almost all humans, a materially different threshold.

reviews.rationale: Part holds: by early 2025 Amodei did talk about 2026-2027. The postponement does not hold: the 2023 forecast covered conversational human-likeness, while the 2026-2027 dates cover broadly superhuman AI, which the 2023 remarks placed later anyway. That matches the contract's different-threshold contradiction. 'Mostly' is not established either way.

attribution.note: Marcus restates his own earlier point and endorses it here.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'current tools' and the sense of 'pretty hard', not impossible.

contract.note: Reading the claim as material difficulty producing a basic playable game, with tools from March 2025, is ordinary and fair to Marcus.

evidence.note: Guardian, 11 March 2025. One Grok user hit many bugs and gave up after an hour. This is one anecdote with one tool, so the support is weak.
The same Guardian passage as e1. 'Surprisingly easy' is followed by the same user describing bugs, so it is not real counterevidence. It duplicates e1.

reviews.rationale: The only evidence is anecdotes from one article about one tool (Grok). The results are mixed: some users needed fixes, others got rough versions quickly. The contract requires documented trials across contemporary tools with functional checks, and the packet has none, so the general claim is not settled.
